overview.lead: Cooking makes the food that buffs raiders and adds experience while you level, and the Basic Campfire it lights opens a campsite.

points.text: More Cooking skill unlocks bigger camp kits that hold more camp features.
Many raid foods were reworked for Forever, and several of them need an Iron Oven.

101.summary: What Forever changes for Cooking, how camps work, and how to level it.

steps.text: Eat crafted food while you level. Blizzard says it now gives a small experience bonus as well as stats.
Most buff foods give a 15-minute Well Fed buff plus 5% more experience from kills.
Finish the short questline around level 5 that unlocks camping.

mistakes.mistake: Treating Cooking as a raid-only profession.
mistakes.fix: Crafted food gives a small experience bonus, and most buff foods add 5% more experience from kills, so it helps while you level too.

steps.text: Light a Basic Campfire. It creates a campsite with vendors, repairs, profession workstations and one-hour buffs you get by sitting at the fire.
The Basic kit (Cooking 1) holds 3 camp features, the Journeyman kit 5 and the Expert kit 10. Each player can add one feature per camp.
Kits have a 5-minute cooldown, and all camp features share a 1-hour cooldown. Sit or craft nearby for about a minute and the benefits last an hour.
The first camp objects come from trainers or NPCs at skill 20. Advanced ones come from blueprints that drop from dungeon bosses.

mistakes.mistake: Trying to pitch a camp in a major city.
mistakes.fix: Camps cannot be placed in major cities.

mistakes.mistake: Expecting a camp buff to stack with the class buff it matches.
mistakes.fix: Camp buffs do not stack with class buffs.

steps.text: Cooking follows the same rank ladder as the other professions, up to 300. Artisan Cooking comes from the Clamlette Surprise quest at level 35.
Get the Journeyman Campfire blueprint from Lord Serpentis in Wailing Caverns.
Kill Cookie in the Deadmines for the skill-140 Cookie's Feast blueprint and Cookie's Stirring Rod, a wand that gives +25% cooking speed.
Buy Cooking recipes from the Azeroth Commerce Authority with Merchant's Favor.

Four Legacy perks help a cook: Master Chef gives extra cooking results, Gourmand makes food buffs last longer, the Field Guide perk shortens the camp-feature cooldown and Reagent Economy removes vendor reagents for tier-1 camp features.

mistakes.mistake: Looking for an Artisan Cooking trainer.
mistakes.fix: Artisan Cooking comes from the Clamlette Surprise quest at level 35.

201.summary: The reworked raid foods, the Iron Oven, and what sells.

steps.text: For spell damage, cook Nightfin Soup (+22) or Baked Salmon and Lobster Stew (+28).
Grilled Squid and Hot Smoked Bass give +1% crit, Mightfish Steak +40 attack power, Smoked Desert Dumplings +20 Strength and Dirge's Chops +25 Stamina.
For healers, cook Sage's Tea: +44 healing, at Cooking 250.
Plan on an Iron Oven. Icy Veins says Dirge's Chops, Mightfish Steak and Grilled Squid need one, and it needs Cooking 300.

mistakes.mistake: Expecting to cook Mightfish Steak at a Basic Campfire.
mistakes.fix: Icy Veins says it also needs an Iron Oven, a camp object that needs Cooking 300.
Smoked Desert Dumplings (+20 Strength) and Dirge's Chops (+25 Stamina) keep their stats.

steps.text: Foods that need an Iron Oven, such as Dirge's Chops, Mightfish Steak and Grilled Squid, may stay scarce while few cooks have one. Trading is subject to Blizzard policy.

mistakes.fix: Crafted food also gives a small experience bonus, and most buff foods add 5% more experience from kills, so players who are leveling buy food too.
